title: Opposed success directions
observation: Rule 17 describes pools, rule 35 requires a high roll, and rule 188 works examples with an inclusive low target. The preface recommends 188 for combat while openly acknowledging the conflict.
consequence: The direction and context must be specified before a die total has meaning. The preface gives a preference but no complete unified test.

title: A class conversion changes a roll-under cutoff
observation: Rule 188 prints 35 C3 as 17.7 C2. Reversing rule 45 on the increasing branch yields 17.4825728. Subtracting ten and rounding to a whole die value gives seven, while the printed example gives eight.
consequence: A roll of 8 succeeds under the worked example and fails under the recalculated threshold.

title: Two success fractions
observation: The preface says two thirds and rule 35 says 66 percent. With an assumed percentage-of-maximum reading, both give a threshold of 12 on 3d6. Their thresholds differ on 25d6, at 100 and 99 respectively.
consequence: The larger pool is an editorial stress test, not a source example. The denominator remains unspecified.

title: Opposite operations preserve different things
observation: Under the additive and multiplicative trades, shortening a 40 C2 LS to 20 from an initially equal PL produces 60 or 80 PL. One route preserves a sum and the other a product.
consequence: The choices are allowed alternatives. There is no unique PL given only the initial and final LS.

title: A higher lifespan rating can produce fewer years
observation: Reading the 22 − C2 relation as applying below 20 and the multiplier two as applying from 20 gives 129.52 years at 19 C2 LS but 98.56 at 20. The 22 − C2 statement is printed without a restriction.
consequence: The piecewise reading reconciles the wording locally and still loses monotonicity. A different calibration would be an editorial amendment.

title: Several mappings called C0 Psyche
observation: C1 DP of 100 can yield 50 C0 by the logarithmic quotient or 100 by identity, depending on the comparison. Other examples use C2/2 or C3/3.
consequence: The statistic and type of subject must accompany C0. A universal conversion table would erase source conditions.

title: C0 immortality has two formulas
observation: At 20 C1 DP, equivalent to 49.28095 C2, the two #31 proposals yield about 246.4 and 40. The author discusses the character types for which each might be appropriate.
consequence: A proposed domain qualification exists. Rules for selecting the form on every new character do not follow.

title: Two budgets for one HERO comparison
observation: At 100 C1 DP the proposed HERO total is 1000 under the linear C1 relation and 1600 under the C3 logarithmic relation. Rule 122 calls the 600-point difference an uncertainty.
consequence: A range of estimates cannot determine which budget to spend.

title: Rounding a baseline changes the next conversion
observation: Rule 8 gives 12.54321 C1, 16 C2 and 28.55 C3 together. Full precision gives 16.08799 C2 and 28.55264 C3. Treating the printed integer 16 as exact yields 28.17766 C3.
consequence: Carry the unrounded C1 result for cross-scale work. The rounded 16 can still explain the 4 AMBS example.

title: Two motion laws in an overlapping context
observation: If a mutant’s #64 movement includes running, 20 C2 DP gives 10 mph by the inverse of #39 and 49.28 mph by #64 at the equivalent C3 DP.
consequence: Mode-specific applicability could reconcile them. The reader cannot infer that restriction from these statements alone.

title: Two speeds for one warp number
observation: Rule 30 permits both 2^z − 1 and 2^(z−1). At z = 2 they give 3 and 2 times light speed.
consequence: A warp number and craft size do not select one speed.

title: Technology formulas fail even at their stated special case
observation: Rule 145 gives C2 PL = TL² and TL = √(C2 PL)/2. It proposes an exception at TL 6 and C2 PL 36, although the latter formula returns TL 3 there.
consequence: The ordinary inverse of the first relation would omit division by two. The source gives no replacement for either equation.

title: The subtracted damage die
observation: For the same 49 C3 PL input, #118’s two named pool readings give 7d6 or 6d6. Rule 146 supplies an additional square-of-C2-DP pool for mutants.
consequence: Effect type and a branch must be selected. A claim that every hit uses one universal pool would conceal the conflict.

title: Infinite exponent assigned a finite value
observation: For an alphabet position of one, #200 assigns a finite 100 CA to a base of two raised to infinity. Ordinary positive integer powers of two grow without bound. The separate class-conversion sequence beginning at 100 CA is algebraically valid.
consequence: The first mark can serve as fictional notation. It fails if read as a mathematical limit.

title: One celestial diameter, multiple numerical inputs
observation: Rule 25 permits miles or kilometers for diameter in the same logarithmic expression with unchanged coefficient. The numeric rating changes when the same physical length is expressed in the other unit.
consequence: A unit must be fixed for reproducible comparisons. No unit-invariant physical law is supplied.

title: Overlapping alphabetic multiplier conditions
observation: In #55, index + 1 can be both even and divisible by three. #58 separately fixes ten times the index in one use. The illustrated X, Y and Z do not resolve every possible overlap.
consequence: Applying a single alphabet chart to all figures would require undocumented precedence and scope.

title: Two estimates for the same appearance rating
observation: At 20 C2 the later rule gives 9 while the earlier C3/(π+1) expression gives about 11.90. Rule 197 expressly compares the two.
consequence: The catalogue preserves both as game calibrations. Neither provides evidence about actual people.

title: An effect called permanent may wear off
observation: Rule 45 contrasts temporary effects with effects paid for by demoting a creator’s class status. The creator may recover the previous status after a supposedly permanent effect wears off naturally.
consequence: An example of changing status exists. Its duration and expiry procedure remain open.

title: A phasing percentage can exceed one hundred
observation: Rule 53 calls the triangular expression a percentage. At total 150 C2 and base 10 it evaluates to 120 percent.
consequence: The literal formula works as a scale but needs a bound or a further interpretation before it can represent an ordinary probability.

title: Relative magnitudes disagree even for equal souls
observation: At equal C2 DP and the example modifier 1, #34’s comparison yields 0.1. Equal class ratings in a direct ratio give 1. The author recognizes discrepancies between comparison models.
consequence: The number of comparable entities and a scale ratio cannot be assumed to mean the same thing.
